meta.title: Who really said "What you do makes a difference, and you have to decide what kind of difference you want to make"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Genuinely Jane Goodall's message and widely credited to her, but no book, speech, or interview is documented for the exact wording. An honest look at the sourcing.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'What you do makes a difference, and you have to decide what kind of difference you want to make'?
meta.ogDescription: Credited to Jane Goodall (even by her own institute) and true to her message, yet no primary source documents the exact line. Attributed, not verified.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.sourceLine: Universally credited to Jane Goodall — and embraced by the Jane Goodall Institute itself — the line sits squarely inside her lifelong message about individual impact and hope. But no primary source (a specific book, speech, or interview, with a date) has ever been documented for this exact wording; it circulates in quote compilations without a citation, and neither Quote Investigator nor Wikiquote’s sourced section pins it to an origin.

source.excerpt: You cannot get through a single day without having an impact on the world around you. What you do makes a difference, and you have to decide what kind of difference you want to make.
trail: The Jane Goodall Institute of Canada lists the line among Goodall’s guiding quotes — but gives no book, speech, or date for it.
Quote compilations from Goodreads to news round-ups of her most famous quotes all reproduce it with the same absence of any citation.

Wikiquote’s sourced section does not carry this exact line; the closest documented statement is a reworded one from her filmed final message: “every single day you live, you make a difference…and you get to choose the difference that you make.”
Quote Investigator has not published a trace of this quotation, so no earliest-attestation date is on record.
source.excerptNote: The two-sentence form above is the version most often reproduced; the shorter “What you do makes a difference…” is simply its second half. No compilation traces either to a dated primary source.

If it were drawn from one of her books or talks it would be in copyright to her estate and publishers; because no source can be identified, we assert no rights status rather than guess.

author.name: Jane Goodall
author.kicker: The true voice behind the message
author.heading: Jane Goodall
author.bio: Dame Jane Goodall (1934–2025) transformed the study of chimpanzees through her decades of fieldwork at Gombe, Tanzania, beginning in 1960, and later became one of the world’s most recognizable voices for conservation and hope. Through the Jane Goodall Institute and its youth program Roots & Shoots, she spent her final decades urging ordinary people to recognize the daily impact of their choices. The idea that every individual makes a difference — and gets to decide what kind — was the through-line of her public message for more than thirty years.

misattribution.heading: The catch: it's real, but sourceless
misattribution.intro: This is not a case of the wrong author — the thought is unmistakably Goodall’s and she voiced it for decades. The catch is that a line reproduced on posters, mugs, and institute pages has never been anchored to a documented origin.

items.why: The quote is frequently shared as if lifted from one of her books (Reason for Hope is sometimes guessed), but no compilation supplies a title, page, or edition, and the primary source remains unlocated. Treat any book-and-page citation you see as unverified.

Wikiquote’s sourced section documents a similar idea in different words — “every single day you live, you make a difference…and you get to choose the difference that you make” — which is sometimes conflated with the classic wording. They express the same thought but are not the same sentence.

misattribution.truthLine: Genuine to Jane Goodall in spirit and consistent with everything she said — but honestly attributed, not verified, because no dated primary source for the exact wording has ever been shown. See the Jane Goodall Institute’s own listing, which carries the line without a citation.

context.heading: Why the line resonates
lead: The sentence distills the argument Goodall returned to again and again in her later career: that hope is not passive, and that agency is unavoidable. If you cannot pass a day without leaving some mark on the world, then the only real question is what kind of mark — a framing that turned a scientist’s observation into a call to personal responsibility.

That message was the engine of her youth program, Roots & Shoots, and it is why the quote spread so widely after her death in October 2025. Its authenticity is not really in doubt; only its paper trail is.
detailsBody: Quotle marks a quote verified only when the specific work containing the exact wording can be shown. Here, despite near-total agreement on the author, no book, essay, speech transcript, or dated interview has been located that carries the sentence as worded — not even on the Jane Goodall Institute’s own pages, which reproduce it without a source.

This is the honest middle ground: strong, uncontested attribution to Goodall; no evidence it originated with anyone else; but no primary source to lift it into the verified tier. If a dated original surfaces, this page will be upgraded.
context.pull: The point isn't whether you make a difference — it's deciding which kind.
